thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert: ap-southeast-2/gpu-fleet-7 at 99% allocation, pending queue growing rapidly, 429s increasing from 0.1% -> 18% in 7m. Autoscaler firing but nodes failing to join. Paging oncall.

jesse (oncall): grabbing dashboard. spike concentrated on /v1/generate and /v1/chat-stream for model 'redwood-2-medium'. Multiple large orgs impacted (org_731, org_844).

rachel (sre): Any config or policy deploys in the last hour? Could be a tokenbucket change or tier policy problem.

jesse (oncall): I see a tier-policy rollout started ~05:40 UTC to shift some traffic to "economy" bucket; looking for PR.

ivan (eng-runtime): that was me — small roll to test economy tier limits. It should only affect internal test orgs, but I'll check rollout percentage.

jesse (oncall): logs: ```
2026-01-15T05:39:58Z policy-service: apply-tier-mapping commit=93b1ed env=prod rollout=20% target=orgs:internal,partner
2026-01-15T05:40:12Z proxy: route=/v1/generate bucket=economy allowed=1 rejected=224 code=429
2026-01-15T05:40:40Z runtime: tokenbucket:economy refill=2 burst=5 dropped=1800
2026-01-15T05:41:01Z autoscaler: scale-loop desired=12 pool=gpu-fleet-7 reason=backlog
2026-01-15T05:41:25Z cloud-provisioner: create-instance inst=621 request=4
2026-01-15T05:41:58Z cloud-provisioner: kube-join-failure inst=621 error=cert-rotation-timeout
```

rachel (sre): Wait, policy-service shows target includes partner orgs due to wildcard match in selector. That explains org_731 getting economy mapping. economy bucket refill=2 is way too low for partner traffic.

ivan (eng-runtime): ugh — my rollout selector used "orgs:*partner*" instead of exact match. Bad wildcard. That matches enterprise partner namespaces. Rolling that change back now.

priya (prod-ops): Meanwhile cloud-provisioner cert rotation timeout seems to be a separate infra flake — ben, any idea?

ben (infra): We're seeing CA cert propagation delays in ap-southeast-2 region due to recent maintenance. New nodes can't complete kubelet TLS handshake until CA is present. Provider says propagation will finish ~20m, but we can warm a spare pool in another region.

jesse (oncall): Immediate mitigations: 1) abort tier rollout (ivan) 2) bump economy tokenbucket temporarily for affected orgs (rachel/ivan) 3) targeted spill to warm spare pool in ap-southeast-1 or eu-west for partner orgs (priya/ben) 4) inform customers (luis). Which can we do fastest?

ivan (eng-runtime): aborting rollout: policy-service rollback -> in progress.

deploy-bot: (deploy) policy-rollback: commit=93b1ed -> SUCCESS (00:00:24)

rachel (sre): Bumping tokenbucket for economy for affected org IDs only: set refill=30 burst=80 for org_731/org_844. Applying now via runtime override.

deploy-bot: (deploy) runtime-override: tokenbucket.economy.orgs=[org_731,org_844] refill=30 burst=80 -> SUCCESS (00:00:10)

jesse (oncall): Observability: immediate drop in 429s for those orgs from ~22% -> 3% within 60s. Overall cluster 429s fell to 6%. Queue length is decreasing but still elevated.

priya (prod-ops): Initiating spill to warm-spare ap-southeast-1 for partner traffic. Note: this requires cross-region certificate mapping and may increase p50 by ~30-80ms. Priya proceeding.

deploy-bot: (deploy) route-spill: orgs=[org_731,org_844] -> warm-spare-ap-southeast-1 -> PENDING

deploy-bot: (deploy) route-spill applied -> SUCCESS (00:02:35)

ben (infra): spare pool warmed. Kube join errors in ap-southeast-2 are still happening due to CA lag. Provider estimates full propagation in ~18m. Quota available in spare region.

luis (customer-success): I've messaged the affected enterprise contacts: brief note that engineers are mitigating, routing some traffic to a warmed pool, and we will follow up with an RCA. They asked for an ETA on full restoration.

jesse (oncall): ETA: service for impacted orgs should be stable for new requests now (we confirmed), backlog clearing within 20-30m. Full restoration for original region depends on cert propagation (~18m).

rachel (sre): Root cause summary so far: 1) wildcard selector in tier-policy rollout accidentally matched partner orgs, mapping them to a low-capacity economy bucket. 2) runtime bucket configuration was too aggressive for that traffic. 3) concurrent infra CA propagation in region prevented autoscaler from rapidly attaching new nodes, amplifying the impact.

ivan (eng-runtime): Follow-ups I'm opening: PR#5102 fix policy selector validation, PR#5103 add rollout-sanity check to detect wildcard hits against high-volume orgs, and PR#5104 improve per-org override UI.

ben (infra): I'll follow up with provider on CA propagation SLA and add an alert for kube-join-cert-timeouts > 30s. Also proposal: keep a small warm spare in-region to avoid cross-region spill for short CA blips.

priya (prod-ops): Action items: - revoke wildcard selector patterns in policy templates - add a pre-rollout check that simulates selector match counts - add playbook steps for rapid per-org spill and communicating customer ETA

luis (customer-success): Drafting customer-facing summary to send after postmortem. Will include mitigation timeline and what we're doing to prevent recurrence.

jesse (oncall): Thanks all. Monitoring closely for 30m. If stable, we'll close this thread. Great response. :thumbsup:
